source.text: וְאֶת־בֵּיתוֹ֙ בָּנָ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה שְׁלֹ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וַיְכַ֖ל אֶת־כָּל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And his house built Solomon thirteen years, and he finished all his house.

en.L: But his own house Solomon built [over] thirteen years, and he finished all his house.
en.B: Solomon was building his own palace for thirteen years, and then he finished the whole of it.
en.R: It took Solomon thirteen years to build his own palace. Then the whole palace was finished.

decisions.choice: his house: the king's palace, a group of buildings
decisions.reason: The word "house" is used for Yahweh's temple in chapter 6 and for the king's own dwelling here. The palace was a complex of buildings: the House of the Forest of Lebanon, the Hall of Pillars, the Hall of Judgment, the king's own house and a house for Pharaoh's daughter (verses 2-8).

decisions.choice: his own house: set against the house of Yahweh just finished
decisions.reason: The verse puts "his house" first, which sets it beside the temple completed in 6:37-38 after seven years. The writer gives no comment on the thirteen years. 9:10 counts twenty years for both buildings together.

decisions.choice: the palace work told between the temple and its furnishings
decisions.reason: The account of the palace (verses 1-12) stands between the building of the temple (chapter 6) and the bronze and gold work for it (verses 13-51). 2 Chronicles, which retells this history, leaves the palace description out.

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's house and keep "house" for Yahweh's, as in 3:1. Literal keeps "house".

source.text: וַיִּ֜בֶן אֶת־בֵּ֣ית׀יַ֣עַר הַלְּבָנ֗וֹן מֵאָ֨ה אַמָּ֤ה אָרְכּוֹ֙ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה קוֹמָת֑וֹ עַ֗ל אַרְבָּעָה֙ טוּרֵי֙ עַמּוּדֵ֣י אֲרָזִ֔ים וּכְרֻת֥וֹת אֲרָזִ֖ים עַל־הָעַמּוּדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he built [the] house of [the] forest of the Lebanon; a hundred cubit[s] its length and fifty cubit[s] its breadth and thirty cubit[s] its height, on four rows of pillars of cedars, and beams of cedars on the pillars.

en.L: And he built the House of the Forest of Lebanon; its length [was] a hundred cubits and its width fifty cubits and its height thirty cubits, on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams on the pillars.
en.B: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon {{units:about 150 feet|a hundred cubits}} long, {{units:about 75 feet|fifty cubits}} wide and {{units:about 45 feet|thirty cubits}} high. It stood on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams laid on the pillars.
en.R: He also built the hall called the House of the Forest of Lebanon. It was {{units:about 150 feet|a hundred cubits}} long, {{units:about 75 feet|fifty cubits}} wide and {{units:about 45 feet|thirty cubits}} high. It stood on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams laid across the tops of the pillars.

decisions.choice: the House of the Forest of Lebanon: a great hall named for its cedar pillars
decisions.reason: The rows of cedar pillars from Lebanon (5:20) stood like the trunks of a forest, which gave the building its name. Solomon later kept gold shields and gold vessels in it (10:17, 21), and Isaiah 22:8 speaks of the weapons stored in "the house of the forest".

decisions.choice: four rows of pillars
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has four rows. The ancient Greek translation has three, which fits verse 3 if its forty-five, fifteen to a row, counts the pillars. The Hebrew is followed here; how the building was laid out is not certain.

decisions.choice: cubit: about 18 inches
decisions.reason: The cubit was the length from the elbow to the tip of the fingers, about 18 inches (Genesis 6:15). The hall was about 150 by 75 feet, and 45 feet high, larger in floor area than the temple (6:2).

decisions.choice: modern measures, with cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measurements in feet, with the cubits as the reader's alternative. Literal keeps the cubits.

source.text: וְסָפֻ֣ן בָּאֶ֗רֶז מִמַּ֨עַל֙ עַל־הַצְּלָעֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הָֽעַמּוּדִ֔ים אַרְבָּעִ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑ה חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר הַטּֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [it was] paneled with cedar from above over the side-chambers which [were] on the pillars, forty and five; fifteen the row.

en.L: And [it was] covered with cedar above, over the side rooms that [were] on the pillars, forty-five; fifteen [to] the row.
en.B: It was roofed with cedar above the side rooms that rested on the pillars, forty-five rooms, fifteen in each row.
en.R: Above the pillars there were side rooms, forty-five of them, fifteen in each row, and they had a cedar roof.

decisions.choice: covered with cedar: roofed or paneled with cedar boards
decisions.reason: The same verb describes the cedar roof and paneling of the temple (6:9, 15). Here it is the cedar covering over the upper part of the hall.

decisions.choice: the side rooms
decisions.reason: The word means "side" or "rib". In 6:5-8 it names the side rooms built against the temple, and it is taken in that sense here: rooms in the upper part of the hall, resting on the pillars. It may instead mean beams or planks laid on the pillars.

decisions.choice: forty-five, fifteen to a row: counting the side rooms
decisions.reason: The number follows "the side rooms" and is taken to count them, in three rows of fifteen (compare the three tiers of verse 4). It could also count the pillars, which would fit three rows of pillars (see verse 2).

decisions.choice: rooms
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats "rooms" after the number to show what is being counted (m3).

source.text: וּשְׁקֻפִ֖ים שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה טוּרִ֑ים וּמֶחֱזָ֥ה אֶל־מֶחֱזָ֖ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And window-frames [were] three rows, and window to window three times.

en.L: And [there were] window frames [in] three rows, and window [was] opposite window three times.
en.B: There were window frames in three rows, and window faced window in three tiers.
en.R: There were three rows of windows. On each of the three levels, the windows on one side faced the windows on the other side.

decisions.choice: window frames: framed openings
decisions.reason: The word is rare. In 6:4 a related phrase describes the temple's windows. Here it seems to mean windows with heavy frames, though it may mean the beams that framed them.

decisions.choice: window opposite window three times: windows facing each other on three levels
decisions.reason: The windows were set across from one another, on the two long sides of the hall, in three tiers.

decisions.choice: the windows on one side faced the windows on the other side
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "window to window" as windows facing each other across the hall (m2).

source.text: וְכָל־הַפְּתָחִ֥ים וְהַמְּזוּז֖וֹת רְבֻעִ֣ים שָׁ֑קֶף וּמ֧וּל מֶחֱזָ֛ה אֶל־מֶחֱזָ֖ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And all the doorways and the doorposts [were] squared [in] frame, and front of window to window three times.

en.L: And all the doorways and the doorposts [were] square in frame, and in front, window [was] opposite window three times.
en.B: All the doorways and doorposts had square frames, and in front, window faced window in three tiers.
en.R: All the doorways and their posts had square frames. Here too, at the front, windows faced each other on all three levels.

decisions.choice: square in frame: with rectangular frames
alternatives: the doorposts were squared with beams
decisions.reason: The doorways had squared frames, using a word from the same root as "window frames" in verse 4. The ancient Greek translation reads this phrase differently, and the exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: in front, window opposite window: the pattern of verse 4 repeated at the doorways
decisions.reason: The words repeat the end of verse 4. They seem to say that the openings at the front, near the doors, were set facing each other in the same three tiers.

decisions.choice: Here too
decisions.reason: Readable marks that the pattern of verse 4 is repeated.

source.text: וְאֵ֨ת אוּלָ֤ם הָֽעַמּוּדִים֙ עָשָׂ֔ה חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ אָרְכּ֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה רָחְבּ֑וֹ וְאוּלָם֙ עַל־פְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וְעַמֻּדִ֥ים וְעָ֖ב עַל־פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] porch of the pillars he made; fifty cubit[s] its length and thirty cubit[s] its breadth; and a porch [was] on [the] face of them, and pillars and a canopy on [the] face of them.

en.L: And he made the hall of pillars; its length [was] fifty cubits and its width thirty cubits, and a porch [was] in front of them, and pillars and a canopy in front of them.
en.B: He made the Hall of Pillars {{units:about 75 feet|fifty cubits}} long and {{units:about 45 feet|thirty cubits}} wide. There was a porch in front of it, and pillars with a canopy in front of that.
en.R: He made the Hall of Pillars {{units:about 75 feet|fifty cubits}} long and {{units:about 45 feet|thirty cubits}} wide. In front of it was a porch with more pillars and a roof that stuck out over them.

decisions.choice: hall: a hall or porch with pillars
decisions.reason: The word is the same as the porch at the front of the temple (6:3). Here the first use names a whole building, a hall with columns, and the second a smaller porch in front of it.

decisions.choice: canopy: an overhanging roof
decisions.reason: The word is rare in buildings and its sense is uncertain. It probably means a projecting roof or eaves over the front pillars (in Ezekiel 41:25-26 a related word seems to name a canopy of wood). Others take it as a threshold or a step.

decisions.choice: in front of them: in front of the hall's pillars
decisions.reason: "Them" refers back to the pillars of the hall. The porch, with its own pillars and canopy, stood in front of the main colonnade.

decisions.choice: the Hall of Pillars
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable write the building's name with capitals, as with the House of the Forest of Lebanon (verse 2). Readable says "a roof that stuck out" for the canopy (m2).

source.text: וְאוּלָ֤ם הַכִּסֵּא֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁפָּט־שָׁ֔ם אֻלָ֥ם הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט עָשָׂ֑ה וְסָפ֣וּן בָּאֶ֔רֶז מֵהַקַּרְקַ֖ע עַד־הַקַּרְקָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] porch of the throne where he would judge there, [the] porch of the judgment, he made; and [it was] paneled with cedar from the floor to the floor.

en.L: And he made the hall of the throne where he would judge, the hall of judgment; and [it was] covered with cedar from the floor to the floor.
en.B: He made the Hall of the Throne, where he was to judge, the Hall of Judgment. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
en.R: He made the Throne Hall, where he would judge cases. It was called the Hall of Judgment, and it was lined with cedar from the floor all the way up to the ceiling.

decisions.choice: the hall of the throne, the hall of judgment: one hall with two names
decisions.reason: The king was the highest judge, and people brought their cases to him (3:16-28; 2 Samuel 15:2-4). Here Solomon sat on his throne to give judgment. The throne itself is described in 10:18-20.

decisions.choice: from the floor to the floor: over the whole wall, up to the floor above
alternatives: from one floor to the other floor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "floor". It probably means from the floor of the hall to the floor of the story above, that is, to the ceiling. The ancient Syriac translation reads "to the rafters", which some think was the original wording.

decisions.choice: to the ceiling
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ceiling" for the second "floor", the floor above (m2). Literal keeps the repeated word.

source.text: וּבֵיתוֹ֩ אֲשֶׁר־יֵ֨שֶׁב שָׁ֜ם חָצֵ֣ר הָאַחֶ֗רֶת מִבֵּית֙ לָֽאוּלָ֔ם כַּמַּֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה הָיָ֑ה וּבַ֜יִת יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לְבַת־פַּרְעֹה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָקַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כָּאוּלָ֖ם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And his house where he would dwell there, [the] other court, from inside to the porch, like the work the this was; and a house he would make for [the] daughter of Pharaoh whom had taken Solomon, like the porch the this.

en.L: And his house where he would live, [in] the other court, inward from the hall, was of the same workmanship; and he made a house for the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Solomon had taken [as wife], like this hall.
en.B: His own house where he was to live, in the other courtyard further in from the hall, was built the same way. Solomon also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married.
en.R: The house where Solomon himself would live was in another courtyard behind the hall, and it was built in the same way. Solomon also built a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married.

decisions.choice: the other court, inward from the hall: a courtyard further inside
decisions.reason: The king's living quarters stood in a separate courtyard behind the public halls, so that people with business came first to the Hall of Judgment.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh's daughter: the wife of 3:1
decisions.reason: Solomon had brought her to the city of David until his building was done (3:1). 9:24 tells that she moved into this house. 2 Chronicles 8:11 gives the reason: a place where the ark had been was holy.

decisions.choice: whom Solomon had taken: whom he had married
decisions.reason: "To take" a woman is the ordinary way of saying to marry her (Genesis 24:67).

decisions.choice: Solomon himself
decisions.reason: Readable names Solomon, the "he" of the verse.

source.text: כָּל־אֵ֜לֶּה אֲבָנִ֤ים יְקָרֹת֙ כְּמִדֹּ֣ת גָּזִ֔ית מְגֹרָר֥וֹת בַּמְּגֵרָ֖ה מִבַּ֣יִת וּמִח֑וּץ וּמִמַּסָּד֙ עַד־הַטְּפָח֔וֹת וּמִח֖וּץ עַד־הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַגְּדוֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: All these [were] stones costly, by [the] measurements of hewn stone, sawn with the saw from inside and from outside, and from [the] foundation to the copings, and from outside to the court the great.

en.L: All these [were of] costly stones, cut to measure, sawn with saws inside and outside, from the foundation to the coping, and from the outside to the great court.
en.B: All these buildings were made of costly stones, cut to size and sawn on their inner and outer faces, from the foundation up to the top course, and from the outside as far as the great courtyard.
en.R: All these buildings were made of fine, expensive blocks of stone, cut to size and sawn smooth on the inside and the outside. This stone was used from the foundations to the top of the walls, and all the way out to the great courtyard.

decisions.choice: costly stones: fine building stone of high quality
decisions.reason: "Costly" or "precious" stones here are not gems but large, well-cut blocks, the kind quarried for the temple's foundation (5:31).

decisions.choice: cut to measure, sawn with saws: dressed stone with smooth faces
decisions.reason: The stones were cut to set sizes, and their faces were sawn smooth, both the faces that showed inside and those that showed outside.

decisions.choice: the copings: the top course of the wall
decisions.reason: The word is related to "handbreadth" and is found only here in this sense. It seems to name the top layer of stone or the projecting stones under the roof.

decisions.choice: from the outside to the great court: the whole extent of the buildings
decisions.reason: The phrase seems to mean that the same quality of stone was used all the way out to the great courtyard that surrounded the buildings (verse 12).

decisions.choice: buildings
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "these buildings" for "all these", which refers back to the buildings of verses 2-8.

source.text: וּמְיֻסָּ֕ד אֲבָנִ֥ים יְקָר֖וֹת אֲבָנִ֣ים גְּדֹל֑וֹת אַבְנֵי֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר אַמּ֔וֹת וְאַבְנֵ֖י שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה אַמּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And [it was] founded [with] stones costly, stones great, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.

en.L: And the foundation [was of] costly stones, large stones, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
en.B: The foundations were laid with costly stones, large stones, some measuring {{units:about 15 feet|ten cubits}} and some {{units:about 12 feet|eight cubits}}.
en.R: The foundations were made of huge, expensive stones. Some were {{units:about 15 feet|ten cubits}} long, and others {{units:about 12 feet|eight cubits}}.

decisions.choice: costly stones, large stones: huge cut blocks for the foundations
decisions.reason: Very large cut blocks were laid as foundations for the temple too (5:31). Stones of this size needed great labor to quarry and move (5:29).

decisions.choice: stones of ten cubits: measured in length
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the measure, not which side is meant. Length is the natural sense for building blocks.

decisions.choice: long
decisions.reason: Readable says the measurement is the stones' length (m2).

source.text: וּמִלְמַ֗עְלָה אֲבָנִ֧ים יְקָר֛וֹת כְּמִדּ֥וֹת גָּזִ֖ית וָאָֽרֶז׃

records.literal_gloss: And from above [were] stones costly, by [the] measurements of hewn stone, and cedar.

en.L: And above [were] costly stones, cut to measure, and cedar.
en.B: Above them were costly stones cut to size, and cedar beams.
en.R: On top of the foundations were more fine stones cut to size, along with cedar beams.

decisions.choice: above: the walls built on the foundations
decisions.reason: "Above" sets the upper walls against the foundations of verse 10. They were built of cut stone with cedar.

decisions.choice: cedar: courses of cedar beams laid in the stone walls
decisions.reason: Verse 12 and 6:36 describe walls of three courses of stone and one of cedar beams. Wooden beams laid between the courses were a known way to strengthen stone walls.

decisions.choice: cedar beams
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "beams", since the cedar was laid in beams (m2).

source.text: וְחָצֵ֨ר הַגְּדוֹלָ֜ה סָבִ֗יב שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ טוּרִ֣ים גָּזִ֔ית וְט֖וּר כְּרֻתֹ֣ת אֲרָזִ֑ים וְלַחֲצַ֧ר בֵּית־יְהוָ֛ה הַפְּנִימִ֖ית וּלְאֻלָ֥ם הַבָּֽיִת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And the court the great all around, three rows of hewn stone and a row of beams of cedars; and for [the] court of [the] house of Yahweh the inner, and for [the] porch of the house.

en.L: And the great court all around [had] three rows of cut stone and a row of cedar beams, as also the inner court of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the porch of the house.
en.B: The great courtyard had walls all around of three courses of cut stone and one course of cedar beams, like the inner courtyard of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the porch of the house.
en.R: The wall around the great courtyard was built with three layers of cut stone and then a layer of cedar beams. The inner courtyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple was built the same way, and so was the porch of the temple.

decisions.choice: the great court: the large courtyard around the royal buildings
decisions.reason: The great courtyard enclosed the palace buildings, and probably the temple courtyard too, as one royal and sacred area.

decisions.choice: the inner court of the house of Yahweh: built in the same way
decisions.reason: 6:36 uses the same words for the temple's inner courtyard: three courses of cut stone and one course of cedar beams.

decisions.choice: the porch of the house: the temple's porch
decisions.reason: Right after "the house of Yahweh", "the house" most naturally means the temple, whose porch is described in 6:3. It could instead mean a porch of the palace.

decisions.choice: courses (Balanced); layers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "rows". In a wall these are courses of stone laid one on another, so Balanced says "courses" and Readable "layers". Readable says "temple" for the house of Yahweh, as in 3:1.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַיִּקַּ֥ח אֶת־חִירָ֖ם מִצֹּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Solomon and took Hiram from Tyre.

en.L: And King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.
en.B: King Solomon sent for Hiram and brought him from Tyre.
en.R: King Solomon sent for a man named Hiram and had him brought from the city of Tyre.

decisions.choice: Hiram: a craftsman, not Hiram the king of Tyre
decisions.reason: This Hiram has the same name as the king of Tyre who supplied Solomon with timber (5:15-26), but he is a bronze worker (verse 14). 2 Chronicles 2:12-13 calls him Huram-abi and says the king of Tyre sent him.

decisions.choice: sent and brought: a step back in time
decisions.reason: The story now turns from the palace back to the temple. Hiram's bronze work belongs to the seven years of the temple building (6:38), so this sending came before the palace was finished.

decisions.choice: a man named; the city of
decisions.reason: Readable introduces Hiram as a new person and says that Tyre was a city.

source.text: בֶּן־אִשָּׁה֩ אַלְמָנָ֨ה ה֜וּא מִמַּטֵּ֣ה נַפְתָּלִ֗י וְאָבִ֣יו אִישׁ־צֹרִי֮ חֹרֵ֣שׁ נְחֹשֶׁת֒ וַ֠יִּמָּלֵא אֶת־הַחָכְמָ֤ה וְאֶת־הַתְּבוּנָה֙ וְאֶת־הַדַּ֔עַת לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כָּל־מְלָאכָ֖ה בַּנְּחֹ֑שֶׁת וַיָּבוֹא֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת־כָּל־מְלַאכְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] son of a woman, a widow, he [was] from [the] tribe of Naphtali, and his father [was] a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze; and he was filled with the wisdom and the understanding and the knowledge to do any work in bronze; and he came to the king Solomon and did all his work.

en.L: He [was] the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father [was] a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. And he was filled with wisdom and understanding and knowledge to do any work in bronze; and he came to King Solomon and did all his work.
en.B: He was a widow's son from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father had been a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Hiram was full of wisdom, understanding and knowledge for doing every kind of work in bronze. He came to King Solomon and did all his work.
en.R: His mother was a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father had been a man from Tyre who worked in bronze. Hiram was very wise and skilled, and he knew how to do every kind of bronze work. He came to King Solomon and did all the work the king gave him.

decisions.choice: filled with wisdom, understanding and knowledge: like Bezalel
decisions.reason: The same three words describe Bezalel, who made the tabernacle and its furnishings (Exodus 31:3; 35:31). Hiram is presented as the Bezalel of the temple. "Wisdom" here is practical skill in a craft.

decisions.choice: a widow of Naphtali: 2 Chronicles 2:13 says of Dan
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 2:13 calls his mother a woman "of the daughters of Dan" and says he was skilled in gold, silver, iron, stone, wood and fabrics as well as bronze. The two may both be true if his mother was of Dan by birth and had married into Naphtali, but the text does not explain the difference.

decisions.choice: a worker in bronze: describing the father
alternatives: Hiram was a worker in bronze
decisions.reason: The words follow "a man of Tyre" and are taken to describe Hiram's father, a bronze worker whose craft the son learned. They may describe Hiram himself.

decisions.choice: had been
decisions.reason: Since the mother is a widow, Balanced and Readable say the father "had been" a man of Tyre. Readable says "the work the king gave him" for "all his work", the work Solomon wanted done.

source.text: וַיָּ֛צַר אֶת־שְׁנֵ֥י הָעַמּוּדִ֖ים נְחֹ֑שֶׁת שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה אַמָּ֗ה קוֹמַת֙ הָעַמּ֣וּד הָאֶחָ֔ד וְחוּט֙ שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אַמָּ֔ה יָסֹ֖ב אֶת־הָעַמּ֥וּד הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he fashioned the two pillars [of] bronze; eighteen cubit[s] [was] [the] height of the pillar the one, and a line of twelve cubit[s] would go around the pillar the second.

en.L: And he cast the two pillars of bronze; eighteen cubits [was] the height of the one pillar, and a line of twelve cubits went around the second pillar.
en.B: He cast the two bronze pillars. Each pillar was {{units:about 27 feet|eighteen cubits}} high, and it took a line of {{units:about 18 feet|twelve cubits}} to go around it.
en.R: Hiram cast two bronze pillars. Each one was {{units:about 27 feet|eighteen cubits}} tall and {{units:about 18 feet|twelve cubits}} around.

decisions.choice: the one pillar ... the second pillar: each pillar
decisions.reason: Hebrew can give one measure for "the one" and the other for "the second" while meaning both. The two pillars were a pair of the same size (verses 16-22).

decisions.choice: fashioned: cast in a mold
decisions.reason: The verb means to shape or form. Here the pillars were cast in molds of clay (verse 46).

decisions.choice: the pillars told again in 2 Chronicles 3:15 and Jeremiah 52:21
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 3:15 gives the pillars a length of thirty-five cubits, perhaps the two together, or reckoned another way; the reason for the difference is not known. Jeremiah 52:21 agrees with eighteen and twelve cubits and adds that each pillar was hollow, with metal four fingers thick.

decisions.choice: each
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "each" for "the one ... the second" (m1). Readable names Hiram as the one who made the pillars and the bronze pieces that follow (verses 23, 27, 36, 38), since "he" could be taken as Solomon.

source.text: וּשְׁתֵּ֨י כֹתָרֹ֜ת עָשָׂ֗ה לָתֵ֛ת עַל־רָאשֵׁ֥י הָֽעַמּוּדִ֖ים מֻצַ֣ק נְחֹ֑שֶׁת חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֗וֹת קוֹמַת֙ הַכֹּתֶ֣רֶת הָאֶחָ֔ת וְחָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת קוֹמַ֖ת הַכֹּתֶ֥רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And two capitals he made to put on [the] tops of the pillars, cast of bronze; five cubits [the] height of the capital the one, and five cubits [the] height of the capital the second.

en.L: And he made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars; the height of the one capital [was] five cubits, and the height of the second capital five cubits.
en.B: He also made two capitals of cast bronze for the tops of the pillars. One capital was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} high, and the other capital was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} high.
en.R: He also made two bronze tops, called capitals, to set on the tops of the pillars. Each capital was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} tall.

decisions.choice: capitals: the crowning pieces on top of the pillars
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "to surround" or "crown". It names the large decorated top of each pillar.

decisions.choice: five cubits: 2 Kings 25:17 has three
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:22 agrees with five cubits. 2 Kings 25:17, telling how the Babylonians broke up the pillars, gives three cubits. The difference may come from copying, or from measuring only part of the capital.

decisions.choice: bronze tops, called capitals
decisions.reason: Readable explains the building word "capital" the first time it appears.

source.text: שְׂבָכִ֞ים מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה שְׂבָכָ֗ה גְּדִלִים֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה שַׁרְשְׁר֔וֹת לַכֹּ֣תָרֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָעַמּוּדִ֑ים שִׁבְעָה֙ לַכֹּתֶ֣רֶת הָאֶחָ֔ת וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה לַכֹּתֶ֥רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: Networks, work of network, wreaths, work of chains, for the capitals which [were] on [the] top of the pillars; seven for the capital the one and seven for the capital the second.

en.L: Nets of network, wreaths of chain work, for the capitals that [were] on top of the pillars: seven for the one capital and seven for the second capital.
en.B: There were nets of lattice work and wreaths of chain work for the capitals on top of the pillars, seven for one capital and seven for the other.
en.R: The capitals on top of the pillars were decorated with lattice work like a net and with chains twisted like wreaths, seven for each capital.

decisions.choice: networks: a lattice of crossing bands
decisions.reason: The word means a net or a lattice. It describes metal work in a crisscross pattern laid over the rounded part of the capitals (verses 18, 20, 41-42; 2 Kings 1:2 uses it of a lattice window).

decisions.choice: wreaths of chain work: twisted chains
decisions.reason: The first word is used of twisted cords or tassels (Deuteronomy 22:12). Here it describes chains twisted together and hung as wreaths on the capitals.

decisions.choice: seven for each capital: the number of what is not said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say whether seven counts the nets, the wreaths or both. The ancient Greek translation reads differently here, and the details of the design are uncertain.

decisions.choice: decorated with lattice work like a net and with chains twisted like wreaths
decisions.reason: Readable puts the capitals first and describes the two kinds of decoration in plain words.

source.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת־הָעַמּוּדִ֑ים וּשְׁנֵי֩ טוּרִ֨ים סָבִ֜יב עַל־הַשְּׂבָכָ֣ה הָאֶחָ֗ת לְכַסּ֤וֹת אֶת־הַכֹּֽתָרֹת֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָֽרִמֹּנִ֔ים וְכֵ֣ן עָשָׂ֔ה לַכֹּתֶ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made the pillars, and two rows all around on the network the one to cover the capitals which [were] on [the] top of the pomegranates; and so he did for the capital the second.

en.L: And he made the pomegranates, two rows all around on the one network, to cover the capitals that [were] on top of the pillars; and so he did for the second capital.
en.B: He made the pomegranates in two rows all around on the one network, to cover the capitals on top of the pillars, and he did the same for the other capital.
en.R: He made two rows of bronze pomegranates to go all around the net on one capital, to cover the top of the pillar. He did the same for the other capital.

decisions.choice: made the pomegranates ... on top of the pillars
alternatives: he made the pillars; and two rows ... to cover the capitals that were on top of the pomegranates
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text as handed down reads "he made the pillars ... the capitals on top of the pomegranates", which seems to have the two words in each other's places: capitals stand on pillars, not on pomegranates, and verses 20 and 42 put the pomegranates in two rows on the networks. Some Hebrew manuscripts have the words the other way round, and that order is followed here.

decisions.choice: pomegranates: bronze fruit as ornaments
decisions.reason: Pomegranates were a sign of the land's fruitfulness (Numbers 13:23; Deuteronomy 8:8). Pomegranates of colored yarn hung from the hem of the high priest's robe (Exodus 28:33-34).

decisions.choice: bronze
decisions.reason: Readable says the pomegranates were bronze, as all this work was (verse 45).

source.text: וְכֹֽתָרֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָעַמּוּדִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה שׁוּשַׁ֣ן בָּֽאוּלָ֑ם אַרְבַּ֖ע אַמּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] capitals which [were] on [the] top of the pillars [were] work of lily, in the porch, four cubits.

en.L: And the capitals that [were] on top of the pillars [were] lily work, at the porch, four cubits.
en.B: The capitals on top of the pillars at the porch were lily work, {{units:about 6 feet|four cubits}} high.
en.R: The capitals on top of the pillars at the porch were shaped like lilies, {{units:about 6 feet|four cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: lily: a lily or lotus flower
decisions.reason: The word names a large flower, the lily or perhaps the lotus, a common shape in carving and metal work. The rim of the Sea had the same shape (verse 26).

decisions.choice: at the porch, four cubits: the lily work, four cubits high
alternatives: lily work, as in the porch
the lily work was four cubits of the capital's five
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and unclear. It is taken here to mean that the capitals at the porch had lily work four cubits high, perhaps the upper part of the five-cubit capital (verse 16). It may instead mean "lily work like that in the porch", or give a measure of something else.

source.text: וְכֹתָרֹ֗ת עַל־שְׁנֵי֙ הָֽעַמּוּדִ֔ים גַּם־מִמַּ֨עַל֙ מִלְּעֻמַּ֣ת הַבֶּ֔טֶן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְעֵ֣בֶר הַשְּׂבָכָ֑ה וְהָרִמּוֹנִ֤ים מָאתַ֨יִם֙ טֻרִ֣ים סָבִ֔יב עַ֖ל הַכֹּתֶ֥רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And capitals on [the] two pillars also above, close to the bulge which [was] beside the network; and the pomegranates [were] two hundred, rows all around, on the capital the second.

en.L: And the capitals on the two pillars [were] also above, close to the rounded part that [was] beside the network; and the pomegranates [were] two hundred, in rows all around, on the second capital [too].
en.B: The capitals on the two pillars were also above, close to the rounded part beside the network. There were two hundred pomegranates in rows all around, on the other capital as well.
en.R: The capitals on both pillars had a rounded, bowl-shaped part next to the net. There were two hundred pomegranates in rows all around each capital.

decisions.choice: the bulge: the rounded, bowl-shaped part of the capital
decisions.reason: The word means "belly". It seems to name the swelling, rounded part of each capital, called the "bowls" of the capitals in verse 41.

decisions.choice: two hundred pomegranates on each capital
decisions.reason: Two hundred is the number for each capital, in two rows; verse 42 counts four hundred for the two. Jeremiah 52:23 says ninety-six could be seen from the sides, and a hundred went around on the network.

decisions.choice: bowl-shaped
decisions.reason: Readable adds "bowl-shaped" from verse 41 to explain the rounded part (m1).

source.text: וַיָּ֨קֶם֙ אֶת־הָֽעַמֻּדִ֔ים לְאֻלָ֖ם הַֽהֵיכָ֑ל וַיָּ֜קֶם אֶת־הָעַמּ֣וּד הַיְמָנִ֗י וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶת־שְׁמוֹ֙ יָכִ֔ין וַיָּ֨קֶם֙ אֶת־הָעַמּ֣וּד הַשְּׂמָאלִ֔י וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ בֹּֽעַז׃

records.literal_gloss: And he set up the pillars at [the] porch of the temple; and he set up the pillar the right and called its name Jachin; and he set up the pillar the left and called its name Boaz.

en.L: And he set up the pillars at the porch of the temple; and he set up the right pillar and called its name Jachin, and he set up the left pillar and called its name Boaz.
en.B: He erected the pillars at the temple porch. The pillar on the right he set up and named Jachin, and the pillar on the left he set up and named Boaz.
en.R: He put up the pillars at the porch of the temple. He named the pillar on the right Jachin, which means "He establishes", and he named the pillar on the left Boaz, which may mean "In him is strength".

decisions.choice: Jachin: "he establishes" or "he will establish"
decisions.reason: The name is a verb form meaning "he makes firm" or "he will make firm". The one who establishes is probably Yahweh, who promised to establish David's house and throne (2 Samuel 7:12-13, 16; 1 Kings 9:5).

decisions.choice: Boaz: probably "in him is strength"
decisions.reason: The meaning of this name is less clear. It is usually explained as "in him (or it) is strength", or "in strength". Boaz is also the name of David's ancestor (Ruth 4:21-22). The two names together may form a short saying about Yahweh making the king's throne firm in strength.

decisions.choice: right and left: seen from inside the temple
decisions.reason: The temple faced east (Ezekiel 8:16). The right side here is probably the south, as in verse 39, so Jachin stood on the south and Boaz on the north. The pillars stood free beside the entrance, not holding up the roof.

decisions.choice: the pillars told again in 2 Chronicles 3:17
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 3:17 gives the same names and says the pillars stood "in front of the temple". The book does not explain the names.

decisions.choice: which means "He establishes"; which may mean "In him is strength"
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely meanings of the names, since they are meant to say something. The second is marked "may" because its sense is less certain (m2).

source.text: וְעַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ הָעַמּוּדִ֖ים מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה שׁוֹשָׁ֑ן וַתִּתֹּ֖ם מְלֶ֥אכֶת הָעַמּוּדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And on [the] top of the pillars [was] work of lily; and was completed the work of the pillars.

en.L: And on top of the pillars [was] lily work; and the work of the pillars was completed.
en.B: On top of the pillars was lily work. So the work on the pillars was finished.
en.R: The tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. That finished the work on the pillars.

decisions.choice: lily work: repeating verse 19
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the account of the pillars with the lily work of verse 19.

decisions.choice: was completed: finished in every part
decisions.reason: The same verb closes the gold covering of the temple (6:22). It marks the end of one section of the work.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם מוּצָ֑ק עֶ֣שֶׂר בָּ֠אַמָּה מִשְּׂפָת֨וֹ עַד־שְׂפָת֜וֹ עָגֹ֣ל׀סָבִ֗יב וְחָמֵ֤שׁ בָּֽאַמָּה֙ קוֹמָת֔וֹ וְקָו֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה יָסֹ֥ב אֹת֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made the sea cast, ten by the cubit from its lip to its lip, round all around, and five by the cubit its height, and a line of thirty by the cubit would go around it all around.

en.L: And he made the sea of cast [metal], ten cubits from its brim to its brim, round all around, and its height [was] five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits went around it all around.
en.B: He made the Sea of cast metal. It was round, {{units:about 15 feet|ten cubits}} from brim to brim and {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} high, and it took a line of {{units:about 45 feet|thirty cubits}} to measure around it.
en.R: Hiram made a huge round tank of cast bronze called the Sea. It was {{units:about 15 feet|ten cubits}} across from rim to rim and {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} high, and it measured {{units:about 45 feet|thirty cubits}} around.

decisions.choice: the sea: a great basin of water
decisions.reason: The great bronze basin was called "the Sea" because of its size. 2 Chronicles 4:6 says it was for the priests to wash in. It took the place of the bronze basin of the tabernacle (Exodus 30:17-21).

decisions.choice: ten across and thirty around: measures in round numbers
decisions.reason: A circle ten cubits across measures a little more than thirty-one around. The writer gives round numbers, or the line may have been measured below the brim, which flared outward like a cup (verse 26).

decisions.choice: a line: the word as read
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew spells the word "line" with an extra letter; the reading tradition gives the usual spelling. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the Sea told again in 2 Chronicles 4:2-5
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 4:2 repeats these measurements. It also tells of a bronze altar twenty cubits square (4:1), which Kings does not describe here but mentions in 8:64.

decisions.choice: a huge round tank of cast bronze called the Sea
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Sea was, so that readers do not picture a body of water (m1).

source.text: וּפְקָעִים֩ מִתַּ֨חַת לִשְׂפָת֤וֹ׀סָבִיב֙ סֹבְבִ֣ים אֹת֔וֹ עֶ֚שֶׂר בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה מַקִּפִ֥ים אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם סָבִ֑יב שְׁנֵ֤י טוּרִים֙ הַפְּקָעִ֔ים יְצֻקִ֖ים בִּיצֻקָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And gourds under its lip all around [were] going around it, ten to the cubit, encircling the sea all around; two rows the gourds, cast in its casting.

en.L: And gourds under its brim all around encircled it, ten to a cubit, going around the sea all around; the gourds [were in] two rows, cast when it was cast.
en.B: Under its brim, gourds went all around it, ten {{units:to every 18 inches|to a cubit}}, encircling the Sea. The gourds were in two rows, cast in one piece with it.
en.R: Below the rim, two rows of gourd-shaped knobs ran all the way around the Sea, ten {{units:to every 18 inches|to a cubit}}. They were cast in one piece with the Sea.

decisions.choice: gourds: round ornaments shaped like gourds
decisions.reason: The same word describes the carved cedar of the temple (6:18). A related word names the wild gourds of 2 Kings 4:39. These were rounded knobs cast on the outside of the basin.

decisions.choice: gourds: 2 Chronicles 4:3 has oxen
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 4:3 has "the likeness of oxen" in place of gourds. The two Hebrew words look alike, and one may have been read for the other.

decisions.choice: cast in its casting: made in the same pour as the basin
decisions.reason: The gourds were not added afterwards but cast together with the Sea.

decisions.choice: gourd-shaped knobs
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gourds were (m1).

source.text: עֹמֵ֞ד עַל־שְׁנֵ֧י עָשָׂ֣ר בָּקָ֗ר שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה פֹנִ֣ים׀צָפ֡וֹנָה וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֩ פֹנִ֨ים׀יָ֜מָּה וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה׀פֹּנִ֣ים נֶ֗גְבָּה וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פֹּנִ֣ים מִזְרָ֔חָה וְהַיָּ֥ם עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְכָל־אֲחֹֽרֵיהֶ֖ם בָּֽיְתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Standing on twelve oxen, three facing northward, and three facing westward, and three facing southward, and three facing eastward; and the sea [was] on them above, and all their hindquarters [were] inward.

en.L: [It was] standing on twelve oxen, three facing north and three facing west and three facing south and three facing east; and the sea [was] on them, above, and all their hindquarters [were] toward the inside.
en.B: It stood on twelve oxen: three faced north, three west, three south and three east. The Sea was set on top of them, and their hindquarters were all toward the center.
en.R: The Sea stood on twelve bronze oxen. Three faced north, three faced west, three faced south and three faced east. The Sea rested on their backs, and their back ends all pointed toward the center.

decisions.choice: twelve oxen, three toward each direction
decisions.reason: The text gives no meaning for the twelve oxen. The number matches the twelve tribes, which camped three on each side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2), but the writer does not draw that link.

decisions.choice: the oxen later removed
decisions.reason: King Ahaz later took the Sea down from the bronze oxen and set it on a stone base (2 Kings 16:17), and the Babylonians broke up the Sea and carried off its bronze (2 Kings 25:13, 16).

decisions.choice: bronze
decisions.reason: Readable says the oxen were bronze (verses 44-45).

source.text: וְעָבְי֣וֹ טֶ֔פַח וּשְׂפָת֛וֹ כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה שְׂפַת־כּ֖וֹס פֶּ֣רַח שׁוֹשָׁ֑ן אַלְפַּ֥יִם בַּ֖ת יָכִֽיל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And its thickness [was] a handbreadth, and its lip like [the] work of [the] lip of a cup, a blossom of lily; two thousand bath[s] it would hold.

en.L: And its thickness [was] a handbreadth, and its brim [was] made like the brim of a cup, [like] a lily blossom; it held two thousand baths.
en.B: It was {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}} thick, and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held {{units:about 12,000 gallons|two thousand baths}}.
en.R: Its walls were {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}} thick, and its rim curved outward like the rim of a cup or the petals of a lily. It held {{units:about 12,000 gallons|two thousand baths}} of water.

decisions.choice: handbreadth, bath: a hand's width and a measure of liquid
decisions.reason: A handbreadth was the width of four fingers, about 3 inches. The bath was a liquid measure equal to the ephah, perhaps about 6 gallons; its exact size is not known, so the total is an estimate (Ezekiel 45:11).

decisions.choice: two thousand baths: 2 Chronicles 4:5 has three thousand
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 4:5 says the Sea "received and held three thousand baths". The reason for the difference is not known: it may come from copying, or the Chronicler may give what the Sea could hold when filled to the brim.

decisions.choice: like the brim of a cup, a lily blossom: a rim that flared outward
decisions.reason: The brim curved outward like the lip of a drinking cup or the open petals of a flower.

decisions.choice: about 12,000 gallons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the volume in gallons, with the baths as the alternative; the figure is approximate (m1). Readable adds "of water".

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ אֶת־הַמְּכֹנ֛וֹת עֶ֖שֶׂר נְחֹ֑שֶׁת אַרְבַּ֣ע בָּאַמָּ֗ה אֹ֚רֶךְ הַמְּכוֹנָ֣ה הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וְאַרְבַּ֤ע בָּֽאַמָּה֙ רָחְבָּ֔הּ וְשָׁלֹ֥שׁ בָּאַמָּ֖ה קוֹמָתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made the stands, ten, [of] bronze; four by the cubit [the] length of the stand the one, and four by the cubit its breadth, and three by the cubit its height.

en.L: And he made the ten stands of bronze; four cubits [was] the length of each stand, and four cubits its width, and three cubits its height.
en.B: He also made ten bronze stands. Each stand was {{units:about 6 feet|four cubits}} long, {{units:about 6 feet|four cubits}} wide and {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|three cubits}} high.
en.R: Hiram also made ten bronze stands on wheels. Each one was {{units:about 6 feet|four cubits}} long, {{units:about 6 feet|four cubits}} wide and {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|three cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: stands: wheeled carts to carry basins of water
decisions.reason: The word means something set firmly in place, a base or stand. Each of these stands was a square bronze cart on four wheels (verse 30) that carried a basin (verse 38).

decisions.choice: the use of the stands
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 4:6 says the ten basins were for rinsing the parts of the burnt offerings. The wheels let the water be moved around the court.

decisions.choice: 2 Chronicles mentions the stands only briefly
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 4:6 and 4:14 name the basins and the stands but leave out the long description of verses 27-37.

decisions.choice: on wheels
decisions.reason: Readable says at the start that the stands had wheels (verse 30), so that readers can picture them.

source.text: וְזֶ֛ה מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הַמְּכוֹנָ֖ה מִסְגְּרֹ֣ת לָהֶ֑ם וּמִסְגְּרֹ֖ת בֵּ֥ין הַשְׁלַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [was the] work of the stand: panels [belonged] to them, and panels [were] between the crossbars.

en.L: And this [was] the work of the stand: they had panels, and the panels [were] between the crossbars.
en.B: This is how the stands were made: they had panels, and the panels were set between crossbars.
en.R: This is how the stands were built: they had flat side panels set between crossbars.

decisions.choice: panels: flat side pieces held in a frame
decisions.reason: The word means something enclosed or a border. Here it seems to name the flat sides of the stand, set within a frame.

decisions.choice: crossbars: the bars of the framework
decisions.reason: The word is related to the rungs of a ladder or to joints. It probably names the bars or uprights of the frame that held the panels.

decisions.choice: the work of the stand: a description of the stands that follows
decisions.reason: "This" points ahead to the description in verses 28-36, among the hardest passages in the book to follow. Several of its building words are found nowhere else.

source.text: וְעַֽל־הַמִּסְגְּר֞וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀בֵּ֣ין הַשְׁלַבִּ֗ים אֲרָי֤וֹת׀בָּקָר֙ וּכְרוּבִ֔ים וְעַל־הַשְׁלַבִּ֖ים כֵּ֣ן מִמָּ֑עַל וּמִתַּ֨חַת֙ לַאֲרָי֣וֹת וְלַבָּקָ֔ר לֹי֖וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה מוֹרָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And on the panels which [were] between the crossbars [were] lions, oxen and cherubim; and on the crossbars a base above; and below the lions and the oxen [were] wreaths, work of hanging.

en.L: And on the panels that [were] between the crossbars [were] lions, oxen and cherubim; and on the crossbars [was] a base above; and below the lions and the oxen [were] wreaths of hanging work.
en.B: On the panels between the crossbars were lions, oxen and cherubim. On the crossbars there was a base above, and below the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
en.R: On the panels between the crossbars were figures of lions, oxen and cherubim. On top of the crossbars was a base. Below the lions and oxen hung decorations shaped like wreaths.

decisions.choice: lions, oxen and cherubim: figures cast on the panels
decisions.reason: Cherubim were winged heavenly creatures that guarded holy things (Genesis 3:24); they were carved on the temple walls (6:29) and stood over the ark (6:23-28; Exodus 25:18-20). Lions also stood beside Solomon's throne (10:19-20).

decisions.choice: a base above
decisions.reason: The word, as the vowels of the Hebrew text read it, means a base or stand, perhaps a support for the basin above the crossbars. With other vowels the same letters mean "likewise": "and on the crossbars likewise, above".

decisions.choice: wreaths of hanging work
decisions.reason: The first word names wreaths or garlands. The second is unclear; it may mean work that hangs down, or work set at a slant.

decisions.choice: figures of
decisions.reason: Readable says these were figures, not living animals.

source.text: וְאַרְבָּעָה֩ אוֹפַנֵּ֨י נְחֹ֜שֶׁת לַמְּכוֹנָ֤ה הָֽאַחַת֙ וְסַרְנֵ֣י נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה פַעֲמֹתָ֖יו כְּתֵפֹ֣ת לָהֶ֑ם מִתַּ֤חַת לַכִּיֹּר֙ הַכְּתֵפֹ֣ת יְצֻק֔וֹת מֵעֵ֥בֶר אִ֖ישׁ לֹיֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And four wheels of bronze [belonged] to the stand the one, and axles of bronze, and its four feet, supports [belonged] to them; from under to the basin [were] the supports, cast, from beside each [were] wreaths.

en.L: And each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze axles, and its four feet had supports; under the basin [were] the supports, cast, with wreaths at the side of each.
en.B: Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles, and its four feet had supports. The supports were cast to sit beneath the basin, and each had wreaths at its side.
en.R: Each stand had four bronze wheels on bronze axles. At its four feet were braces that held up the basin. They were cast in bronze, with wreaths on the side of each one.

decisions.choice: supports: "shoulders" bearing the basin
decisions.reason: The word means "shoulders". It names supports rising from the four feet of the stand to hold up the basin.

decisions.choice: its four feet
decisions.reason: The word can mean "feet" or "corners". The supports were at the four corners of the stand (verse 34).

decisions.choice: from beside each, wreaths
decisions.reason: The last words are brief. They seem to say that wreaths were set at the side of each support.

decisions.choice: braces
decisions.reason: Readable says "braces" for the supports, a plain word for a piece that holds something up. Balanced says "supports".

source.text: וּ֠פִיהוּ מִבֵּ֨ית לַכֹּתֶ֤רֶת וָמַ֨עְלָה֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וּפִ֨יהָ֙ עָגֹ֣ל מַעֲשֵׂה־כֵ֔ן אַמָּ֖ה וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֑ה וְגַם־עַל־פִּ֨יהָ֙ מִקְלָע֔וֹת וּמִסְגְּרֹתֵיהֶ֥ם מְרֻבָּע֖וֹת לֹ֥א עֲגֻלּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And its mouth from inside to the crown and upward [was] by the cubit; and its mouth [was] round, work of a base, a cubit and the half of the cubit; and also on its mouth [were] carvings; and their panels [were] squared, not round.

en.L: And its opening, inside the crown and upward, [was] a cubit; and its opening [was] round, made like a base, a cubit and a half; and also on its opening [were] carvings; and their panels [were] square, not round.
en.B: Its opening, within the crown, rose {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}} upward. The opening was round, made like a pedestal, {{units:about 27 inches|a cubit and a half}} across. There were carvings on its opening, and the panels were square, not round.
en.R: At the top of each stand was an opening for the basin, set inside a crown-like rim and rising {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}}. The opening was round, made like a pedestal, {{units:about 27 inches|a cubit and a half}} across, with carvings on it. The side panels were square, not round.

decisions.choice: its opening: the round mouth at the top of the stand
decisions.reason: The word is "mouth". It seems to name the round opening at the top of the stand into which the basin was set. It may instead be the mouth of the basin itself. This verse is among the least clear in the chapter.

decisions.choice: the crown: a raised rim
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the capitals of the pillars (verse 16). Here it seems to name a raised, crown-shaped rim at the top of the stand.

decisions.choice: a cubit and a half: the width of the opening
decisions.reason: The measure is taken as the width across the round opening. The text does not say which way it was measured.

decisions.choice: carvings: engraved designs
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the carved figures on the temple walls (6:18, 29, 32).

decisions.choice: across
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the measure is the width (m3). Readable adds "for the basin" to say what the opening was for (m1).

source.text: וְאַרְבַּ֣עַת הָאֽוֹפַנִּ֗ים לְמִתַּ֨חַת֙ לַֽמִּסְגְּר֔וֹת וִיד֥וֹת הָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים בַּמְּכוֹנָ֑ה וְקוֹמַת֙ הָאוֹפַ֣ן הָאֶחָ֔ד אַמָּ֖ה וַחֲצִ֥י הָאַמָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the four wheels [were] under the panels, and the hands of the wheels [were] in the stand; and [the] height of the wheel the one [was] a cubit and the half of the cubit.

en.L: And the four wheels [were] under the panels, and the axles of the wheels [were] in the stand; and the height of each wheel [was] a cubit and a half.
en.B: The four wheels were under the panels, and the axles of the wheels were fixed to the stand. Each wheel was {{units:about 27 inches|a cubit and a half}} high.
en.R: The four wheels were under the side panels, and their axles were attached to the stand. Each wheel was {{units:about 27 inches|a cubit and a half}} high.

decisions.choice: the hands of the wheels: the axles
decisions.reason: "Hands" is used for parts that hold something. Here it seems to name the axles, or the brackets that held them, fixed to the frame of the stand.

decisions.choice: a cubit and a half high: about 27 inches
decisions.reason: The wheels were small next to the stand, which was three cubits high (verse 27). The stands were made to be moved about the temple court, not driven like chariots.

source.text: וּמַֽעֲשֵׂה֙ הָא֣וֹפַנִּ֔ים כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה אוֹפַ֣ן הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֑ה יְדוֹתָ֣ם וְגַבֵּיהֶ֗ם וְחִשֻּׁקֵיהֶ֛ם וְחִשֻּׁרֵיהֶ֖ם הַכֹּ֥ל מוּצָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] work of the wheels [was] like [the] work of [the] wheel of the chariot; their hands and their rims and their spokes and their hubs, the all [was] cast.

en.L: And the wheels were made like a chariot wheel; their axles and their rims and their spokes and their hubs [were] all cast.
en.B: The wheels were made the way chariot wheels are made: axles, rims, spokes and hubs, all of cast metal.
en.R: The wheels were built like chariot wheels. Their axles, rims, spokes and hubs were all cast from bronze.

decisions.choice: axles, rims, spokes, hubs: the parts of a wheel
decisions.reason: The last three words are found only here, and their senses come from the picture of a chariot wheel. "Rims" is literally "backs" and "spokes" and "hubs" are words from the root for joining.

decisions.choice: chariot wheel: wheels with spokes
decisions.reason: Chariots were the military vehicles of the time (10:26, 29). Their wheels had spokes, unlike solid cart wheels.

decisions.choice: cast bronze
decisions.reason: Readable says the metal was bronze, as in verse 30.

source.text: וְאַרְבַּ֣ע כְּתֵפ֔וֹת אֶ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פִּנּ֔וֹת הַמְּכֹנָ֖ה הָֽאֶחָ֑ת מִן־הַמְּכֹנָ֖ה כְּתֵפֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And four supports [were] at [the] four corners of the stand the one; from the stand [were] its supports.

en.L: And [there were] four supports at the four corners of each stand; its supports [were] of one piece with the stand.
en.B: There were four supports at the four corners of each stand, and the supports were part of the stand itself.
en.R: Each stand had four braces, one at each corner, made in one piece with the stand.

decisions.choice: from the stand: of one piece with it
decisions.reason: "From the stand" means that the supports were part of the stand, cast with it rather than fixed on afterwards (compare verse 35).

decisions.choice: braces
decisions.reason: As in verse 30.

source.text: וּבְרֹ֣אשׁ הַמְּכוֹנָ֗ה חֲצִ֧י הָאַמָּ֛ה קוֹמָ֖ה עָגֹ֣ל׀סָבִ֑יב וְעַ֨ל רֹ֤אשׁ הַמְּכֹנָה֙ יְדֹתֶ֔יהָ וּמִסְגְּרֹתֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And on [the] top of the stand, half of the cubit [in] height, round all around; and on [the] top of the stand its hands and its panels [were] from it.

en.L: And on top of the stand [was a band], half a cubit [in] height, round all around; and on the top of the stand its brackets and its panels [were] of one piece with it.
en.B: At the top of the stand was a round band {{units:about 9 inches|half a cubit}} high, and at the top of the stand its brackets and panels were one piece with it.
en.R: At the top of the stand was a round band {{units:about 9 inches|half a cubit}} high. The brackets and panels at the top were made in one piece with the stand.

decisions.choice: its hands: brackets at the top of the stand
decisions.reason: "Hands" here are not the axles of verses 32-33 but parts at the top of the stand, probably brackets or stays that held the basin in place.

decisions.choice: half a cubit high, round all around: a band at the top
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the height and shape. It is taken as a round collar or band at the top of the stand, on which the basin rested.

decisions.choice: a band
decisions.reason: Every level supplies "band" to name what was half a cubit high (m2); Literal puts it in brackets.

source.text: וַיְפַתַּ֤ח עַל־הַלֻּחֹת֙ יְדֹתֶ֔יהָ וְעַל֙ מִסְגְּרֹתֶ֔יהָ כְּרוּבִ֖ים אֲרָי֣וֹת וְתִמֹרֹ֑ת כְּמַֽעַר־אִ֥ישׁ וְלֹי֖וֹת סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he engraved on the plates of its hands and on its panels cherubim, lions and palm trees, according to [the] space of each, and wreaths all around.

en.L: And he engraved on the surfaces of its brackets and on its panels cherubim, lions and palm trees, according to the space of each, with wreaths all around.
en.B: On the surfaces of its brackets and on its panels he engraved cherubim, lions and palm trees, as each had space, with wreaths all around.
en.R: Hiram carved cherubim, lions and palm trees on the flat surfaces of the brackets and on the panels, wherever there was room, with wreaths all around them.

decisions.choice: cherubim, lions and palm trees: like the temple walls
decisions.reason: Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the temple walls and doors (6:29, 32, 35). The stands add lions, as on the panels of verse 29.

decisions.choice: according to the space of each: as much as each surface held
alternatives: according to the nakedness of each
decisions.reason: The rare word seems to mean an open or bare space. The figures were fitted to the room on each surface.

decisions.choice: and on its panels: the written and read text
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew and the reading tradition differ slightly in these words. Both give the sense "and on its panels".

source.text: כָּזֹ֣את עָשָׂ֔ה אֵ֖ת עֶ֣שֶׂר הַמְּכֹנ֑וֹת מוּצָ֨ק אֶחָ֜ד מִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֛ת קֶ֥צֶב אֶחָ֖ד לְכֻלָּֽהְנָה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Like this he made the ten stands: one casting, one measure, one shape [belonged] to all of them.

en.L: Like this he made the ten stands: one casting, one measure, one shape [was] for all of them.
en.B: This is how he made the ten stands. All of them were cast alike, with the same size and the same shape.
en.R: He made all ten stands this way. They were all cast alike, and they were the same size and shape.

decisions.choice: one casting, one measure, one shape: all alike
decisions.reason: The repeated "one" says the ten stands were identical, perhaps cast in the same mold.

source.text: וַיַּ֛עַשׂ עֲשָׂרָ֥ה כִיֹּר֖וֹת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת אַרְבָּעִ֨ים בַּ֜ת יָכִ֣יל׀הַכִּיּ֣וֹר הָאֶחָ֗ד אַרְבַּ֤ע בָּֽאַמָּה֙ הַכִּיּ֣וֹר הָאֶחָ֔ד כִּיּ֤וֹר אֶחָד֙ עַל־הַמְּכוֹנָ֣ה הָאַחַ֔ת לְעֶ֖שֶׂר הַמְּכֹנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made ten basins of bronze; forty bath[s] would hold the basin the one; four by the cubit the basin the one; one basin on the stand the one, for [the] ten stands.

en.L: And he made ten bronze basins; each basin held forty baths; each basin [was] four cubits; one basin [was] on each stand of the ten stands.
en.B: He made ten bronze basins. Each basin held {{units:about 240 gallons|forty baths}} and measured {{units:about 6 feet|four cubits}} across, with one basin on each of the ten stands.
en.R: Hiram made ten bronze basins, one for each of the ten stands. Each basin held {{units:about 240 gallons|forty baths}} of water and was {{units:about 6 feet|four cubits}} across.

decisions.choice: basins: bowls of water for washing
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the bronze basin of the tabernacle, where the priests washed (Exodus 30:18). 2 Chronicles 4:6 says these ten basins were for rinsing the parts of the burnt offerings, while the Sea was for the priests.

decisions.choice: four cubits: the width of the basin
decisions.reason: The measure is not said to be width or height. Width across the top is the natural sense, matching the four-cubit stands (verse 27).

decisions.choice: forty baths: about 240 gallons
decisions.reason: On the bath, see verse 26. A basin of this size, full of water, was very heavy, which explains the strong wheeled stands.

decisions.choice: across
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the measure is the width (m2). Readable puts "one for each of the ten stands" first and adds "of water".

source.text: וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הַמְּכֹנ֔וֹת חָמֵ֞שׁ עַל־כֶּ֤תֶף הַבַּ֨יִת֙ מִיָּמִ֔ין וְחָמֵ֛שׁ עַל־כֶּ֥תֶף הַבַּ֖יִת מִשְּׂמֹאל֑וֹ וְאֶת־הַיָּ֗ם נָתַ֞ן מִכֶּ֨תֶף הַבַּ֧יִת הַיְמָנִ֛ית קֵ֖דְמָה מִמּ֥וּל נֶֽגֶב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he put the stands, five on [the] shoulder of the house from [the] right, and five on [the] shoulder of the house from its left; and the sea he put from [the] shoulder of the house the right eastward, from in front of [the] south.

en.L: And he put the stands, five on the right side of the house and five on its left side; and he put the sea on the right side of the house, eastward, toward the south.
en.B: He placed five of the stands on the south side of the house and five on the north side. He put the Sea on the south side of the house, at the southeast corner.
en.R: He put five stands along the south side of the temple and five along the north side. He put the Sea near the southeast corner of the temple.

decisions.choice: right: the south side
decisions.reason: The temple faced east. Seen from the temple looking out, the right side is the south, which the end of the verse makes clear ("toward the south").

decisions.choice: shoulder of the house: its side
decisions.reason: "Shoulder" is used of the side of a building (6:8).

decisions.choice: the Sea placed southeast: as in 2 Chronicles 4:10
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 4:10 gives the same place for the Sea. 2 Chronicles 4:6 adds that five basins were on the south and five on the north.

decisions.choice: south side; north side; southeast corner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "south" and "north" for right and left (m1). Literal keeps "right" and "left".

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ חִיר֔וֹם אֶת־הַ֨כִּיֹּר֔וֹת וְאֶת־הַיָּעִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָק֑וֹת וַיְכַ֣ל חִירָ֗ם לַֽעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And made Hiram the basins and the shovels and the bowls; and finished Hiram to do all the work which he did for the king Solomon [for the] house of Yahweh:

en.L: And Hiram made the basins and the shovels and the bowls. And Hiram finished doing all the work that he did for King Solomon [for] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:
en.B: Hiram also made the basins, the shovels and the sprinkling bowls. So Hiram finished all the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:
en.R: Hiram also made basins, shovels and bowls for sprinkling. So he finished all the work he did for King Solomon on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. This is what he made:

decisions.choice: the basins
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "basins", the word of verse 38. The list in verse 45 and the parallel in 2 Chronicles 4:11 have "pots" at this point, a word that differs by one letter in Hebrew, and "pots" may be the original reading here. The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: shovels and bowls: tools for the altar

decisions.choice: a colon at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The list of verses 41-45 spells out "all the work", so Literal and Balanced end the verse with a colon. Readable adds "This is what he made".

decisions.choice: pots: cooking pots and pails for ashes
decisions.reason: Pots were used to carry away the ashes of the altar (Exodus 27:3) and to boil the meat of sacrifices (Zechariah 14:20-21).

decisions.choice: these: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has letters that would read "the tent"; the reading tradition reads "these", which fits the sentence. 2 Chronicles 4:16 has "all their vessels".

decisions.choice: polished bronze: burnished to a shine
decisions.reason: The verb means to rub or polish. The bronze was burnished to a bright surface.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers tools, vessels and furnishings of every kind. Balanced and Readable say "things" because the list includes pillars and stands; Literal keeps "vessels".

decisions.choice: the thickness of the ground: clay soil used for molds
alternatives: in the foundries of the ground
decisions.reason: The phrase means "thick" or dense ground, that is, clay. The clay of the Jordan valley was suited for making the large molds into which the bronze was poured.

decisions.choice: the plain of the Jordan, between Succoth and Zarethan
decisions.reason: The "plain" is the broad floor of the Jordan valley. Succoth lay east of the Jordan near the Jabbok (Genesis 33:17; Judges 8:5), and Zarethan near the town of Adam (Joshua 3:16). The region had clay, water and fuel, away from the city.

decisions.choice: the king cast them: the king had them cast
decisions.reason: Hiram did the work (verses 40, 45). The king is named as the one who ordered it, as kings were said to build what their workers built.

decisions.choice: had them cast in molds; the towns of
decisions.reason: Readable says the king had the work done, that the clay was used for molds (m1), and that Succoth and Zarethan were towns.

decisions.reason: The verb means to set down or leave. With the second half of the verse it is taken to mean that Solomon did not weigh the vessels. It could mean that he set them in their places.

decisions.choice: the bronze: much of it taken in David's wars
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:8 says David took a great amount of bronze from the cities of Hadadezer, from which Solomon made the Sea, the pillars and the bronze vessels. 1 Chronicles 22:3, 14 say David stored up bronze beyond weighing.

decisions.choice: the golden altar: the altar of incense
decisions.reason: The gold-covered altar stood in the main hall in front of the inner room (6:20-22). Incense was burned on it, as on the altar of incense in the tabernacle (Exodus 30:1-10).

decisions.choice: the bread of the Presence
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were set out on the table before Yahweh each Sabbath (Exodus 25:23-30; Leviticus 24:5-9). The name means bread set "before the face" of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Solomon made: the gold work is credited to the king
decisions.reason: The bronze work was Hiram's (verse 45). The gold furnishings are said to be Solomon's work, made under his command.

decisions.choice: the table: 2 Chronicles 4:8, 19 has ten tables
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 4:19 speaks of "the tables" for the bread of the Presence, and 4:8 says Solomon made ten tables, five on each side. Kings names only one.

decisions.choice: for burning incense; the bread set out before God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the altar was for (m1) and explains "the bread of the Presence" (m2).

decisions.choice: the flowers: blossoms on the lampstands
